question_text: A 32-year-old woman comes to her doctor’s office with abdominal distention, diffuse abdominal pain, and a history of 10–12 bowel movements a day for the last week. She was diagnosed with Crohn’s disease 3 years ago. Today, vitals are normal. Her abdomen is mildly distended and diffusely tender to palpation. A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?
